title: Six top-level tabs; the sixth onward land in More
evidence: TabView (file-01.swift:5-12) declares six .tabItem children: Today, Trends, Workouts, Awards, Sharing, Settings. Six areas against the five-area limit: on iPhone the bar shows four tabs plus a system 'More' tab, and Sharing and Settings become rows in a nested list behind a label that names nothing. The legacy .tabItem form also carries no selection value, so the current area is neither restorable nor deep-linkable. Fix: consolidate to five or fewer areas (for example Settings as a toolbar button on Today) and use TabView(selection:) with Tab(_:systemImage:value:) plus .tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable).

title: Trends tab root has no navigation title
evidence: TrendsView (file-01.swift:16-22) wraps List { Text("This week") } in a NavigationStack with no .navigationTitle, while all five sibling roots (25-29) set one. The Trends screen shows an empty bar with nothing saying where the user is, and any screen pushed from it later gets a back button labelled 'Back'. Fix: .navigationTitle("Trends") on the List.

title: Self-view drag offset in @State strands on cancel
evidence: @State private var dragOffset (file-02.swift:43) is written in .onChanged (54) and reset only inside .onEnded (55-60). SwiftUI does not run .onEnded when the system cancels the drag (incoming call, Control Center, a presented sheet), so the self-view stays displaced by the last translation and the next drag starts from that offset. Source rule; the interruption itself needs a device run. Fix: @GestureState(reset: { _, t in t.animation = UIAccessibility.isReduceMotionEnabled ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.2) }) private var drag: CGSize = .zero, .updating($drag) { v, s, _ in s = v.translation }, and write only corner in .onEnded (the file-04 CallScreen shape).

title: Read-only What's New sheet hard-locks swipe-to-dismiss
evidence: .interactiveDismissDisabled() with no argument (file-02.swift:148) disables swipe-down on WhatsNewSheet, a read-only list of release notes with no input and nothing to lose (122-149). The Done button (143-145) is the only exit, so a reflexive swipe down is refused for no reason. The file-04 TermsUpdateSheet lock is the legitimate case: a required consent step, commented. Fix: delete the modifier.

title: List-plus-detail ships as one column at regular width
evidence: ContentView (file-03.swift:10-23) is a NavigationStack list whose rows push WorkoutDetail (22): list-plus-detail content in a single column, and the file has no NavigationSplitView or adaptive grid. On a regular-width window each row spends the whole width on a name at the leading edge and a calorie number at the trailing edge, and selecting a row replaces the list with a two-line detail. Measurement: 1 column where the content needs 2 (threshold: any occurrence); on a 1024pt window the name and the value are separated by the full row width less the system row insets, and the detail column is 0pt. Fix: NavigationSplitView { List(workouts, selection: $selection) {...} } detail: { if let workout { WorkoutDetail(workout: workout) } else { ContentUnavailableView("Select a Workout", systemImage: "figure.run") } }.

title: Workout list has no empty state
evidence: @State private var workouts: [Workout] = [] (file-03.swift:7) feeds List(workouts) (11) with no isEmpty branch, overlay or ContentUnavailableView anywhere in the view, and nothing populates the array, so the screen is a navigation bar over a blank list. A new user cannot tell empty from a failed load and has no control that creates the first workout. State: empty (no loading or error branch either). Fix: .overlay { if workouts.isEmpty { ContentUnavailableView { Label("No Workouts", systemImage: "figure.run") } description: { Text("Workouts you record appear here.") } actions: { Button("Record a Workout") { startRecording() } } } }.

title: Detail repeats its title as a second large title
evidence: WorkoutDetail sets .navigationTitle(workout.name) (file-03.swift:38) with no display mode, so it inherits the root's large title, and its first content line is Text(workout.name).font(.largeTitle) (32). The workout name renders twice, stacked, both in the 34pt large-title style, and the only data on the screen (calories, line 33) is plain body text under two copies of the heading. Fix: remove line 32, add .navigationBarTitleDisplayMode(.inline), and give the calorie line .font(.title2).

title: ViewThatFits has no candidate that actually fits
evidence: Both ViewThatFits candidates (file-05.swift:11-16 and 17-22) are the same horizontal HStack of a 32x32 icon, label, Spacer and value; the second differs only in spacing 8 instead of 16. Derived: 3 gaps x 8pt = 24pt is the whole saving, so any content that overflows candidate 1 by more than 24pt overflows candidate 2, and the system renders the last candidate regardless. Body text grows about 3.1x at .accessibility5, so on a 320pt window (288pt after .padding() at line 24) label and value truncate. The icon's fixed .frame(width: 32, height: 32) (12, 18) also stays 32pt while the body-sized symbol grows. Configuration: AX5, 320pt window. Fix: make the last candidate VStack(alignment: .leading) { HStack { icon; Text(metric.label) }; Text(metric.value) } and size the icon with @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .body).

title: Workout name pinned to a fixed 120pt column
evidence: Text(workout.name).frame(width: 120, alignment: .leading) (file-06.swift:13-14) answers the size proposal with a number. Derived: at .accessibility5 body text is 53pt (about 3.1x the 17pt default) while the column stays 120pt, so the name breaks mid-word across several lines while the Spacer (15) keeps the rest of the row empty; the icon frame (12) is likewise a fixed 24x24 beside scaling text. Configuration: AX5, every width. Fix: drop the frame and switch layouts on typeSize.isAccessibilitySize: AnyLayout(VStackLayout(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4)) vs AnyLayout(HStackLayout(alignment: .firstTextBaseline, spacing: 12)), with Spacer(minLength: 8) and .layoutPriority(1) on the value (the file-08 WorkoutRow shape).

title: Calorie value sized by the leftover width
evidence: WorkoutRow is HStack { 24pt icon; name at fixed 120pt; Spacer(); calories } (file-06.swift:10-18): the value is placed by whatever the Spacer leaves over. Measurement: on a 1024pt regular-width window, 32pt row padding (.padding() 16 x 2) + 24pt icon + 120pt name + about 3 x 8pt default spacing = about 200pt committed, leaving about 824pt (before system row insets) between the name and a value that is at most 4-5 digits. Threshold: any leftover-sized box with a known maximum; HIGH past 400pt. Configuration: regular width. Fix: remove the fixed frame, use Spacer(minLength: 16) with .monospacedDigit() on the value, and host the list in a NavigationSplitView column so the row is sidebar-width at regular width.

title: Row padding stacked on top of List row insets
evidence: WorkoutRow ends in .padding() (file-06.swift:19) and is the row content of List(workouts) (27). The default 16pt on every side is added inside the system row insets, so row content starts 16pt further in than the separators and the navigation title, and every row gains 32pt of height (2 x 16pt) over a standard single-line row. Fix: replace .padding() with .padding(.vertical, 4), and use .listRowInsets(_:) or .contentMargins(_:_:for:) if a different margin is genuinely wanted.

title: Hamburger drawer is the app's top-level navigation
evidence: TravelRoot (file-07.swift:33-53) reaches its four co-equal areas (Today, Trips, Saved, Settings) only through a line.3.horizontal toolbar button (39-43) that slides in SideMenu (46-50). Nothing on screen says what other areas exist, switching costs 2 taps instead of 1, and the drawer reimplements a tab bar's job with a hand-built scrim and modal trait. Four areas is the tab-bar case (3 to 5). The motion and VoiceOver handling are careful; the model is wrong. Fix: TabView(selection: $area) { Tab("Today", systemImage: "sun.max", value: Area.today) { ... } ... }.tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable), which stays a tab bar on iPhone and becomes a sidebar on iPad (the file-04 TravelRoot shape).

title: Number and decimal pads have no way to dismiss
evidence: Card number uses .keyboardType(.numberPad) (file-09.swift:12) and Amount .decimalPad (14). Neither pad has a return key, and the view has no ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .keyboard), no .scrollDismissesKeyboard, no @FocusState and no tap-to-dismiss, so once either field is focused the keyboard cannot be lowered to reveal the Pay button (16) beneath it. With no @FocusState, a failed submit also cannot move focus to the first bad field. Fix: @FocusState private var focused: Field?, .focused($focused, equals:) on each field, .toolbar { ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .keyboard) { Spacer(); Button("Done") { focused = nil } } } and .scrollDismissesKeyboard(.interactively) on the Form.

title: Payment fields carry no textContentType, so AutoFill is dead
evidence: None of the three TextFields (file-09.swift:10-14) sets .textContentType. Without .creditCardNumber the system offers no saved-card AutoFill on the card field, and without .name the cardholder field gets no suggestion, so every payment is typed by hand: 16 digits plus a name, on the one screen where a typo costs a failed charge. Fix: .textContentType(.name) on Name on card and .textContentType(.creditCardNumber) on Card number.

title: Like and Comments use a bundled second icon set
evidence: The Like and Comments buttons draw Remix Icon assets, Image(isLiked ? "ri-heart-fill" : "ri-heart-line") (file-10.swift:34) and Image("ri-chat-3-line") (42), forced to template mode and a resizable glyph-sized frame, in the same bottom bar as ShareLink's SF Symbol (31). SF Symbols covers both concepts (heart, heart.fill, bubble.left); the bundled glyphs ignore Bold Text, symbol weight and the toolbar's symbol sizing, so their stroke and baseline drift from the share glyph beside them. Fix: Image(systemName: isLiked ? "heart.fill" : "heart").contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace)) and Image(systemName: "bubble.left"), dropping .resizable(), the frame and the glyph @ScaledMetric.

title: Delete All erases every workout on one unconfirmed tap
evidence: The toolbar Button("Delete All", role: .destructive) (file-11.swift:19-22) runs workouts.removeAll() and store.deleteAll() on a single tap: no confirmationDialog, no count, no undo, and the store call is permanent. A stray tap in the navigation bar destroys the whole history irreversibly. Fix: set a pending flag and present .confirmationDialog("Delete All \(workouts.count) Workouts?", isPresented: $isConfirmingDeleteAll, titleVisibility: .visible) { Button("Delete All", role: .destructive) { ... } } message: { Text("This can't be undone.") }.

title: Swipe-delete is permanent, with no undo or rollback
evidence: .onDelete (file-11.swift:12-15) removes the row locally, then calls store.deletePermanently(offsets) in a fire-and-forget Task: no undo, no confirmation, and a full swipe deletes in one gesture. The local removal is optimistic with no failure branch, so a failed store delete leaves the row gone on screen while it still exists in the store, and nobody is told. Fix: keep the removed items and offer an undo for at least 8 seconds before calling the permanent delete (or confirm naming the workout), and restore the rows with a visible message if the store call fails.

title: Overlay bottom bar permanently hides the last list rows
evidence: The Record/Filter bar is attached with .overlay(alignment: .bottom) (file-12.swift:12-20). An overlay does not change the List's safe area, so the scroll content gets no bottom inset for it. Derived: the bar is 16pt padding + a body-height button row (about 22pt) + 16pt = about 54pt at default size, and grows at larger text sizes; that band of the List can never scroll out from under the bar, so the final row is unreachable and its tap target sits under the buttons. Configuration: every size; worse at AX sizes. Fix: .safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom) { HStack { ... }.padding().background(.regularMaterial) }, or the system bar: .toolbar { ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .bottomBar) { ... } }, which also picks up Liquid Glass on iOS 26.

title: Camera controls extend under the status bar and home indicator
evidence: .ignoresSafeArea() (file-13.swift:66) is applied to the whole ZStack, so it expands the control layer (44-64) as well as CameraPreview. The Close button (46-51) is laid out from the physical top edge, under the status bar and Dynamic Island, and the shutter (55-62) sits on the home indicator, where the system home gesture competes for the tap; the VStack's 16pt .padding() (64) is smaller than the top inset of any notched or Dynamic Island iPhone. Fix: move .ignoresSafeArea() onto CameraPreview(session:) only and drop it from the ZStack (the file-04 CaptureScreen shape).

title: Hidden back button kills the interactive pop gesture
evidence: .navigationBarBackButtonHidden(true) (file-14.swift:16) with a hand-rolled ToolbarItem(placement: .topBarLeading) Button calling dismiss() (17-24). Hiding the system back button disables the edge-swipe pop on this pushed screen, so the most-used way back on iOS does nothing (inferred from source; confirm with an edge-swipe in the simulator). The replacement says 'Back' instead of the parent's title and uses chevron.left, which does not mirror in right-to-left layouts. Flow step: list -> WorkoutDetail -> back. Fix: delete lines 16-25 and keep the system back button.

title: Search has no zero-results, empty or loading state
evidence: List(visible) (file-15.swift:15-17) has no overlay or branch for any state but loaded. A query that matches nothing (.searchable, 18) leaves a blank list under the search field with no ContentUnavailableView.search(text:) naming the query; an account with no workouts shows the same blank list, so empty and zero results are conflated into nothing; and while .task { workouts = await store.load() } (20) runs, the screen is blank again. State: zero results, empty, loading. Fix: .overlay { if workouts.isEmpty { ContentUnavailableView("No Workouts", systemImage: "figure.run", description: Text("Workouts you record appear here.")) } else if visible.isEmpty { ContentUnavailableView.search(text: searchText) } }, plus a loading state for the first fetch.

title: Search filter is case- and diacritic-sensitive
evidence: visible filters with $0.name.contains(searchText) (file-15.swift:11). String.contains is a literal match, so typing 'run' does not find 'Morning Run' and 'cafe' does not find 'Café': the user sees no results for a workout that exists. Fix: $0.name.localizedStandardContains(searchText).

title: PillSwitch is a Toggle look-alike with no accessibility bridge
evidence: PillSwitch (file-16.swift:26-41) draws a switch from a Capsule and a Circle and flips the binding in .onTapGesture (40). There is no Button or Toggle underneath and no accessibilityRepresentation, label, value or trait, so VoiceOver, Voice Control and Switch Control cannot find or operate the Push notifications setting (11-16); the row reads as static text. It also has no thumb animation or press state, and sits beside a real Toggle (17) in the same section that looks and behaves differently. Who is affected: VoiceOver, Voice Control and Switch Control users. Fix: Toggle("Push notifications", isOn: $pushEnabled); if the custom look is required, a ToggleStyle whose makeBody wraps a Button and adds .accessibilityRepresentation { Toggle(isOn: configuration.$isOn) { configuration.label } } (the file-04 CheckToggleStyle shape).

title: Near-black text literal is invisible in Dark Mode
evidence: Text("Push notifications").foregroundStyle(Color(red: 0.11, green: 0.11, blue: 0.12)) (file-16.swift:13) is a fixed sRGB literal (about #1C1C1F). In Dark Mode a Form row resolves to secondarySystemGroupedBackground #1C1C1E: relative luminance 0.0118 against 0.0117, contrast 1.00:1 against the 4.5:1 minimum, so the label disappears. Light Mode on white measures 17.00:1. The literal also ignores Increase Contrast, and the sibling Toggle label (17) uses the adaptive label colour. Fix: delete the modifier, or .foregroundStyle(.primary).

title: Digest day Menu draws capsule chrome around a text row
evidence: DigestDayRow's Menu (file-16.swift:49-61) uses a two-line VStack text block widened with .frame(maxWidth: .infinity) as its label and sets no .menuStyle or .buttonStyle. Under the automatic style on iOS 26+ the system draws its tinted menu capsule around that block, so the Form row renders as one oversized accent-coloured pill, and an Xcode 27 build has no opt-out. The file-04 Alert sound row is the correct form. Fix: add .contentShape(.rect) to the label and .menuStyle(.button).buttonStyle(.plain) on the Menu.

title: Compose draft lives in sheet @State; swipe-down erases it
evidence: ComposeSheet holds subject and body in @State (file-17.swift:11-12) inside the presented sheet (45-47). The sheet has no interactiveDismissDisabled, no Cancel with a discard confirmation, and no draft persistence or scenePhase handling, so a reflexive swipe down after typing a long message destroys it with no warning, and so does the system terminating the backgrounded app. The sheet has no Cancel button at all, only Send and the swipe. Flow step: Inbox -> Compose -> Send, step 1 of 1. Fix: own an @Observable ComposeDraft in InboxView and persist it on scenePhase change; in the sheet add .interactiveDismissDisabled(draft.hasContent) and a .cancellationAction Cancel that confirms 'Discard this draft?' when there is content.

title: Send dismisses before the send has a result
evidence: send() (file-17.swift:30-33) starts a detached Task { await api.send(...) } and calls dismiss() on the next line, before the send resolves. There is no in-flight state, no failure branch and no success confirmation: if the send fails, the sheet and its @State draft are already gone, so the message is lost with nothing shown (inferred; api.send's failure mode is elided in the stub). Send is also never disabled, so a double tap during the dismiss animation can send twice. Fix: an isSending flag that disables Send and shows ProgressView(), await the send before dismiss(), and on failure keep the sheet and draft open with an alert that names the cause and offers Try Again.
